attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, listed under reasons OpenAI might struggle.

semantics.note: Keeps 'most', 'to a large degree', 'well-understood' and the 'not clear' hedge on the moat point. It is a combined claim: a firm technical observation joined to an explicitly uncertain commercial judgement.

contract.note: Fair. The contract declines a whole-claim score because the moat sentence only expresses uncertainty, and it keeps the technical evidence as context. That matches policy on hedged language.

evidence.note: Llama 2 paper (July 2023, before the post). Shows reuse of standard published architecture and methods. Bears on the technical sentence only, not on the combined claim.
Alpaca release (March 2023). A public, cheap instruction-tuning recipe, but it depends on a released base model and was licensed for non-commercial use only. Context only.
Imitation-model paper (May 2023). Imitation did not close the capability gap. This limits copyability of frontier capability but does not contradict an uncertain moat statement.

reviews.rationale: The claim joins a technical observation to the hedged 'not clear' moat judgement, and the hedged part cannot be scored. The packet's 2023 technical evidence leans toward accessible methods (e1, e2), and e3 shows a capability gap. All of it is recorded as context only, so the combined claim gets no score.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'appears', 'perhaps', 'roughly in the ballpark', the chat-search exception with '(yet?)', and the investor-patience line. The revenue comparison is hedged, and 'killer app' and 'infinitely patient' are vague.

contract.note: Fair. Any firm test would need the grader to invent a financial tolerance, a standard for 'killer app', or an investor deadline the speaker never gave.

reviews.rationale: The financial comparison is explicitly hedged. 'No killer app' has no measurable standard. 'Investors will not be infinitely patient' names no event or deadline and is close to a truism. Nothing here can be scored, and the packet holds no evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithful to the graded wording 'maybe … probably not … certainly not', with 'so far' as the period. Only the firm 'certainly not hundreds of billions' can be scored.

contract.note: Reading 'made' as revenue earned to date is an ordinary plain reading and is not stretched. Profit would be an even lower bar. The contract fairly sets aside the hedged parts and asks for complete sector coverage on a known accounting basis.

evidence.note: Epoch AI, published 2025, before the evaluation date. Reconstructs revenue for a few companies, e.g. about $1B for OpenAI across all of 2023. It does not cover the whole sector or give a cumulative total through Aug 14, 2023.

reviews.rationale: The scoreable part is that cumulative generative AI revenue through Aug 14, 2023 was below hundreds of billions. e1 covers only selected companies and excludes third-party and infrastructure revenue. The packet establishes no complete sector total or accounting basis, so it does not settle the claim under the contract.
